findings.claim: A plain TRUNCATE of the revisions table never reaches the 55000 revisions guard. PostgreSQL refuses it earlier with 0A000 ('cannot truncate a table referenced in a foreign key constraint'). The 55000 guard is reached only by 'truncate revisions, head' or by CASCADE. These are reading-level conclusions only; runtime is NOT PROVEN. TRUNCATE triggers are statement-level. The row trigger returns NEW, and the statement functions always raise, so they never reach the end without RETURN. Trigger execution needs no EXECUTE privilege at fire time. The multi-statement EXECUTE relies on oneshot per-statement analysis, as the predecessor did. DROP fires no triggers. The verifier's ALTER ... DISABLE TRIGGER fixtures have no pending AFTER events on the altered table, because the RI checks fire at statement end.

A superuser-only ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER "RI_ConstraintTrigger_..." would not be detected. This is compensated by integrity's explicit reference check (.sql:253-260) and the ALWAYS revisions guard. An optional OID-independent check would be: pg_trigger rows whose tgconstraint is one of the three FK oids all have tgenabled='O'.
